problem: Embodied learning pipelines optimize a single stage (data, simulation, training or deployment) and suffer from exogenous off-distribution data, static pre-rendered simulators, separate navigation/manipulation model stacks, and sparse success/failure deployment feedback, so improvement does not persist.
motivation: Embodied competence should come from a closed loop coupling real experience with updates to simulation assets, representations and policies. Prior integrations (GRUtopia, NaVILA) extend only the simulation side or the real-robot side and never route deployment signals back into simulation assets and supervision.
key_idea: Arcadia closes a real-to-sim-to-real lifecycle: robots self-explore real scenes, generatively reconstruct them into editable Isaac Sim assets, train one shared VLM backbone for VLN and VLA on simulated trajectories, and feed structured deployment feedback back into simulation.
insight: The ablation (Tab. 2) shows that removing the static-training-set replacement (task-aligned self-collected data) or the generative scene reconstruction causes the largest drops, and sparse binary feedback also costs accuracy versus the full multi-channel feedback (VLN-CE-Isaac 48.8 vs 50.1). Joint VLN+VLA training costs almost nothing (49.8/87.0 vs 50.1/87.2), suggesting one backbone can serve both tasks. Caveat: the gains over NaVILA are modest, and the feedback effect is small (about 1.4-1.7 SR points in sim).
method: Self-evolving exploration: Isaac ROS + Nvblox SLAM with frontier-based exploration scored by expected entropy reduction; outputs synchronized RGB-D, LiDAR, IMU, odometry and poses in the deployment environment.

Generative scene reconstruction: parse video/point clouds into a 3D scene graph (SpatialLM), synthesize assets from multi-view observations with a Gaussian-splat/InstantMesh-style reconstructor into USD objects, and import them into Isaac Sim.

Shared embodied representation: a Qwen2.5-VL backbone trained jointly on navigation and manipulation with light task-specific decoders; navigation supervision from A* paths in a 7-primitive discrete action space (VLN-CE format), manipulation from RRT trajectories (BridgeData V2 format, OpenVLA-style 7D action de-tokenizer).
Task feedback: step-level signal F_t = λ1 reward + λ2 state-transition magnitude + λ3 perception-consistency loss + λ4 goal-distance loss, for rollout scoring and error localization.
Scene feedback: deployment failures (low-light mapping, unseen objects) are logged and used to instantiate new assets or inject perturbations into the simulator.
Robot feedback: hardware telemetry (joint states, actuator load, comms) yields constraint-violation signals F^R for safety gating and motion-policy adaptation.
Sim-from-Real loop: all feedback channels update assets, dynamics and supervision targets so training and evaluation become one iterative process.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL (7B, fine-tuned) as high-level VLM with NaVILA-style low-level controllers; OpenVLA-style action de-tokenizer for manipulation
setting.training_data: Self-collected task-aligned real-scene data reconstructed into Isaac Sim, with A*/RRT-generated simulated trajectories in VLN-CE/BridgeData formats, plus an auxiliary QA fine-tuning stage as in NaVILA; real-world feedback data for the w/ feedback variant. Data scale not given.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (plus RGB-D, LiDAR, IMU and odometry for mapping/reconstruction)
setting.action_space: 7-primitive discrete navigation control space executed by low-level controllers; 7D end-effector actions for manipulation
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (VLN-CE-Isaac, GRUtopia arm); evaluation also on R2R, RxR, LIBERO, BridgeData V2
setting.privileged: none at test time (feedback from real deployment is used for training)

Real-world results are given as counts/percentages in the text (navigation 46/100, manipulation 27/100 vs NaVILA 13 and OpenVLA 9). The split names for VLN-CE-Isaac and LIBERO are assumed.
results: Arcadia w/ feedback beats NaVILA on all VLN benchmarks (e.g. R2R val-unseen SR 55.9 vs 51.6, VLN-CE-Isaac SR 50.1 vs 45.1), and Arcadia w/o feedback already beats NaVILA by an average of 2.7 SR. On the real Unitree G1 it completed 46% of navigation and 27% of manipulation tasks versus NaVILA 13% and OpenVLA 9%.
limitations: Validated only on the Unitree G1 and Isaac Sim, with a single 7B backbone.
Real-world multi-destination and multi-object compositional tasks remain hard (about 17% success), and the sim gains from feedback are small.

Many details are unspecified (data scale, feedback weights, and how feedback is applied); the manipulation results appear only in a figure and the paper reports no repeated runs or significance tests.
